body: Linux pre-probe of gta_sim tests in local WSL (rustc 1.89 + --ignore-rust-version) fails: bevy_macro_utils 0.19.1 needs rwlock_downgrade (stable only in newer rustc). Not installing 1.95 in WSL; Linux-only test divergence is left to the first real CI run.

One workflow file per badge (clippy, sim, citygen, client, repo-checks) + a local composite setup action, because GitHub status badges cover whole workflows only; rejected: one ci.yml with 5 jobs (single badge) and shields/gist per-job badges (needs a secret).
Trigger on push to all branches except media (+pull_request, workflow_dispatch) because gh here is read-only and cannot open PRs; rejected: push-to-main-only (no pre-merge run, no flip-RED branch).

CI Linux only (ubuntu-latest) with toolchain pinned to 1.95.0; rejected: a Windows matrix (MAW stages already run every gate on Windows locally; Windows doubles wall time and cache footprint against the 10 GB repo cache cap).

Each of the 5 workflows gets a distinct job id (clippy/sim/citygen/client/repo): Swatinem/rust-cache v2 keys on GITHUB_JOB, not the workflow, so a shared job id would make the jobs overwrite each other's target caches. Rejected alternative: one shared-key per workflow (it works too, but a unique job id is simpler and the key stays readable).

flip-RED covers all 5 jobs, one sabotage commit per job, with red/green predicted before the push. Rejected alternative: only clippy + golden (the planner's version), which leaves client gates and repo checks without proof that the job runs its gate.

Added --no-fail-fast to the three cargo test workflows: flip-RED (b) showed cargo stops at the first failing test binary, so a red sim run hid the rest of the suite from the summary (Q2 wants the failing test list). Alternative: plan's plain cargo test, rejected because a Linux-only red would show one binary at a time.
